Stop alternate bearing, fruit drop and small apples

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Apples drop in three waves: after bloom (poor pollination, boron or bees), the June drop (May–June drought and too many fruits competing) and before harvest (heat, ethylene, mites). Fix them with 25–33% pollinizers and a pink-bud boron spray, irrigation in May–June, thinning to one fruit per cluster at pea size (30–40 leaves per fruit), 4–6 calcium chloride sprays, summer pruning for colour, and NAA 10 ppm 10–20 days before expected pre-harvest drop (Dr. YSP UHF, SKUAST-K).

Breaking alternate bearing (on year, off year)

A heavy crop makes seeds that suppress next year's flower buds, so a bumper year is followed by a poor one. Three steps break the cycle:

  1. Thin early: within 10–25 days after petal fall (fruits 8–12 mm), hand-thin to one king fruit per cluster, 15–20 cm apart, about 30–40 leaves per fruit. Or use a registered thinner such as NAA (10–15 ppm) or 6-BA (75–100 ppm) as advised by your university. Avoid carbaryl: it is toxic to bees and restricted. Thinning also roughly doubles fruit size (SKUAST-K, Himachal package of practices).
  2. Protect summer leaves (June–August), when next year's buds form: control Marssonina, Alternaria and mites, and irrigate dry spells.
  3. Reload buds after harvest: 3–5% urea + 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.1–0.2% Solubor on green leaves in October–November.

In the off year cut the post-bloom nitrogen by 50–100%; full nitrogen only produces shoots and shade.

Fruit drop

WaveWhenMain causesWhat helps
Post-bloom dropAfter floweringToo few pollinizers or bees, cold or rain at bloom, boron shortage, spraying at bloom25–33% pollinizers, 4–6 beehives per hectare, boron at pink bud, no bloom sprays
June dropMay–JuneDrought during cell division, too many fruitsIrrigation, pea-stage thinning
Pre-harvest dropBefore pickingHeat, ethylene, mite stressNAA 10 ppm (1 mL Planofix in 4.5 L) 10–20 days before expected drop, mite control; avoid overusing ethephon

Small apples

  • Over-cropping without thinning: the most common cause.
  • Dry spells in May–June (cell division) and August–September (sizing).
  • Spur strains on M.9 in poor soil.
  • Weak roots from root rot, woolly aphid galls or replant disease.
  • Leaf loss from Marssonina, scab or mites before harvest.

Fruit quality: bitter pit, colour and cracking

  • Bitter pit and cork spot (brown sunken spots in the flesh): calcium shortage in the fruit. 4–6 sprays of 0.3–0.5% calcium chloride every 15 days from 2–3 weeks after petal fall; skip above 28–30°C; avoid excess nitrogen and drought swings.
  • Poor red colour: shaded fruit and low altitude. Summer pruning in July–August, high-colour strains in lower belts.
  • Fruit cracking: irregular watering, dry then flooded. Keep moisture even and mulch.

Questions farmers ask

How do I stop alternate bearing in apple?

Thin to one fruit per cluster 10–25 days after petal fall, protect summer leaves, cut off-year nitrogen, and give the October urea + zinc + boron spray.

Why do apple fruits drop in June?

Dry weather in May–June combined with too many fruits competing. Irrigate and thin at pea size.

How do I stop pre-harvest fruit drop in apple?

NAA at 10 ppm (1 mL Planofix in 4.5 L water) 10–20 days before expected drop, plus mite control. Do not overuse ethephon.

What causes bitter pit in apple?

Low calcium in the fruit. Give 4–6 calcium chloride sprays (0.3–0.5%) from 2–3 weeks after petal fall, avoid excess nitrogen and keep watering even.

Why are my apples small?

Usually too many fruits (no thinning), dry spells in May–June or August–September, weak roots or early leaf loss.
